lots.what_it_is: Eight 19th century French transfer-printed earthenware assiettes parlantes (talking plates): four black-printed 1830s-40s romantic scenes (Jamais je n'aime qu'un jour, Apres le Diner, La Lecture, Le Bailli du Village), two hand-coloured plates with blue and yellow floral rims (La Botte de Foin, Dada), one red-rim Droleries No. 6 and one blue-rim Le Langage des Fleurs No. 5 Le Laurier. Probable Creil et Montereau, Choisy-le-Roi or similar factories, but no backstamp is photographed.

asking.price: USD 1,055 for a set of 4 (one rim flake)
asking.venue: 1stDibs dealer listing (P&H Choisy creamware assiettes parlantes, Scheffer series)
asking.note: ASKING, category guide. Page opened: USD 1,055 offer shown, In Stock, description mentions P&H Choisy shield mark and a rim flake to one plate. Rate about 1.50 AUD per USD (approximate, not checked live). Top-end US decorator retail for an earlier named series, so it shows the category has collector interest but grossly overstates what eight mixed plates would make in Tasmania.

lots.guide_summary: No same-item or close entry survives. Nothing sold and nothing unsold. The only surviving entry is one category-guide dealer ask (1stDibs, USD 1,055 for four earlier Choisy plates, about A$1,580 at 1.50), which is not used for the range. Single French plates appear to ask about EUR 20-25 in French classifieds and eBay, but those were snippets only and could not be opened. Rate used: USD 1 = A$1.50 (approximate).
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so both maximums are 0. Gowans API rechecked (shelley/french plates/creil/faience queries): no French talking plates sold at Gowans in the last year. WebSearch was capped this turn so I could not run new Armitage or Australian auction searches. A rough unverified feel: single 19th century talking plates seem to retail about EUR 20-25 in France, so eight might make A$80-200 at a Tasmanian sale, but that is not evidence and sets no bid.
lots.confidence_reason: No maker mark photographed, no sold or unsold results, only a category-guide dealer ask opened.
lots.dropped_entries: leboncoin.fr p-26 (EUR 23-24): page returned 403, snippet only, kept only as a lead and not used. eBay.de 202233059768 (EUR 25): eBay closed to us, snippet only, lead only. LiveAuctioneers 238993977 (estimate USD 950-1,650, set of 8 HBCM 1920s face-card plates): page blocked by Incapsula, unverified, and it is a later, different series with no result, so dropped.
lots.key_photo_findings: Captions read clearly: Jamais je n'aime qu'un jour; Apres le Diner; La Lecture; Le Bailli du Village; La Botte de Foin; Dada; Droleries No. 6 (hare asking the hunter for his permis de chasse); Le Langage des Fleurs, 5 Le Laurier, Gloire. Mixed borders and dates, so a collected assortment, not a set. No backs photographed, so factory marks are unread. No obvious chips in the overview photo at this resolution; the cream-ground Langage des Fleurs plate looks toned and some show general wear and possible crazing.
lots.condition: Appears used but intact from the photos; crazing, staining, rim wear and any restoration not checked; backs unseen.
lots.question_for_armitage: Please check the backs of all eight plates for factory marks (Creil, Montereau, Choisy, Gien, Sarreguemines, HB etc.) and any chips, cracks, hairlines, staining or old repairs.

lots.what_it_is: Shelley fine bone china tea set, Heather pattern 13419 (green Shelley England shield mark), c1945-66: six cups, at least six saucers and six side plates (one spare saucer or plate visible), cake plate with pale green handles, milk jug and sugar bowl, about 22 pieces.

sold.note: SOLD, close. Page opened (API JSON) and I viewed the lot photos: a Shelley tea set in a pink-edged rose pattern, same green Shelley England backstamp, six cups, about 12 saucers/plates, cake plate, milk jug and sugar bowl, so the same make, era and make-up as this lot but a different pattern. Hammer only, premium extra. AUD.

lots.guide_summary: One sold, nothing unsold, no verified asking. The only surviving close entry is a Gowans Shelley tea set of the same make-up (different pattern) at A$130 hammer in October 2025. Category guides at Gowans, not used for the range: six Shelley Begonia trios alone made A$20 (1 bid, July 2026); a single Daffodil Time trio A$40; five mixed Shelley and Royal Albert trios A$60. Those show soft Hobart demand for Shelley trios. All AUD.
lots.working: Keep: lowest surviving close SOLD A$130 / 1.22 = A$106.56, round down to A$105 (all-in about A$128). This rests on one close sale of a different pattern, so treat A$105 as a ceiling, not a target. Flip: likely resale A$130 at a Tasmanian auction, less about 15% seller commission (A$19.50) and A$0 outbound postage (sold locally) = A$110.50; / 2.44 = A$45.29, round down to A$45. Pickup from 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay, inbound freight A$0.
lots.confidence_reason: Backstamp and pattern number read in the photo; only one close SOLD entry (opened, photos checked) and it is a different pattern; the Begonia trios at A$20 pull the other way.
